# Playbook for hf_auction_nerfed

When I see a lot's value to me significantly exceeds the current standing bid, I will bid to compete for it. The margin between my valuation and the current price is what matters, not the absolute estimate.

When I'm in round 1 of 2 for any lot, I will make a substantive opening bid rather than a minimal one. This establishes my interest and may discourage other bidders from escalating aggressively. A bid around one-third of my valuation is reasonable for round 1.

When I'm in round 2 and the standing bid is still well below my valuation, I will raise it by the minimum required amount. This captures value efficiently without overspending.

When calculating whether to bid, I will compare the minimum raise price directly to my valuation. If my valuation exceeds the minimum raise price by a meaningful margin, I bid.

I will track my spending carefully across lots and preserve budget flexibility for remaining lots. I should not commit so heavily to early lots that I cannot bid competitively on later ones.

When I have won multiple lots already, I will not become passive on the final lots. A close score (2-1) is not secure; I should continue bidding on remaining lots where my valuation exceeds the standing bid.

I will not pass on a lot simply because it's the final round. If the value is there, I bid. The game ends after round 2, so I should use my full budget to capture value.

I notice my second episode score was notably lower than my first. This suggests I may have been too conservative or made suboptimal budget decisions. I should bid more aggressively when my valuations clearly exceed standing bids, rather than second-guessing myself.
